title: He didn’t wake up one night and suddenly become “that man.”
paragraphs: He didn’t wake up one night and suddenly become “that man.”

It started earlier.
Quieter.
Hidden.
Before Bathsheba… there was distance.
David—the giant slayer, the worshiper, the man after God’s own heart—slowly drifted. Not in public. Not dramatically.
But subtly.
Scripture says in 2 Samuel 11:1, “At the time when kings go out to battle… David remained in Jerusalem.”
That’s where it cracked.

He stayed when he should’ve gone.
He lingered when he should’ve led.
He got comfortable where he was once called to war.
And idle rooftops create dangerous views.
But here’s what we miss…

Bathsheba wasn’t the beginning of David’s fall.
She was the exposure of a heart that had already loosened its grip on obedience.

Sin rarely explodes overnight.
It erodes… quietly… patiently… convincingly.

A skipped prayer.
A delayed obedience.
A small compromise you promised you could control.
Until one day—you’re standing on a rooftop you never meant to climb.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because David’s story doesn’t end in scandal.
It bends toward repentance.

In Psalm 51, David cries out:
“Create in me a clean heart, O God… restore to me the joy of Your salvation.”

Not excuses.
Not denial.
Brokenness.
And God responds—not by canceling David—but by cleansing him.
That’s the Gospel.

You may have drifted.
You may have stayed when you should’ve fought.
You may already be standing on that rooftop.
But Jesus steps into the story you’re ashamed of.

He doesn’t minimize sin.
He conquers it.
At the cross, He took the full weight of our hidden compromises, our silent drift, our exposed failures—and paid for it in full.
This is your moment.

Not to hide.
Not to justify.
But to return.

Run back.
Fall on grace.
Let Christ rebuild what sin tried to ruin.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
